question: Therapeutic blood range of theophylline in microgram per L is:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Theophylline" -> "bronchodilator" -> "used in asthma/COPD" -> "therapeutic range important" -> "10-20 microgram per L" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Theophylline" -> "narrow therapeutic index" -> "monitoring required" -> "10-20 microgram per L" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Theophylline" -> "risk of toxicity" -> "above 20 microgram per L" -> "therapeutic range below 20" -> "10-20 microgram per L" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Theophylline" -> "effective bronchodilation" -> "achieved at 10-20 microgram per L" -> "below 10 may be ineffective" -> 75%
analysis: The therapeutic blood range of theophylline is a well-established parameter in pharmacology. Theophylline is used primarily as a bronchodilator in the treatment of respiratory diseases such as asthma and COPD. The standard therapeutic range is 10-20 micrograms per liter, which is crucial for achieving effective bronchodilation while minimizing the risk of toxicity. Theophylline has a narrow therapeutic index, meaning that levels above 20 micrograms per liter can lead to toxic effects. Therefore, the most likely correct option based on standard medical knowledge and consensus is 10-20 micrograms per liter.
